teaser.en: One of Kenya's rarest trees hides in the Shimba Hills and Kwale kayas, its white flowers on extraordinarily long tubes.

summary.en: *Mnyandza* is a rare tree of lowland rainforest, with two-lobed leaves and large white flowers on very long tubes. It is listed as Endangered and survives in only a few coastal forests, including the Shimba Hills and the Kwale kayas.

about.en: *Mnyandza* has leaves split into two lobes, like those of the *Bauhinia* or camel's-foot trees it is related to. Its flowers are large and white, sitting at the end of a very long, slender tube, the feature that gives the genus its name, *Gigasiphon*, 'giant tube'.

where.en: It grows in lowland rainforest between about 30 and 600 metres above sea level. On the south coast it is found in the Shimba Hills and the Kwale kaya forests.

uses.en: No particular use for *mnyandza* has been recorded.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *mnyandza*. No Swahili or English name is recorded.

conservation.en: Mnyandza is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is restricted to a few coastal forests, so the protection of the kayas and the Shimba Hills matters for its survival.

reason.en: Camel's foot, with similar two-lobed leaves
Another rare tree of the Shimba Hills forests
